title: Articles and Noun Gender
summary: Definite and indefinite articles with noun gender and singular/plural awareness.
whyItMatters: German articles identify a noun's grammatical gender and help listeners understand whether you mean a specific item, one unspecified item, or several items. Learning the article with every noun creates the foundation for later case grammar.

mentalModel.title: Every noun has a grammatical category
mentalModel.content: German sorts singular nouns into masculine, feminine, or neuter. The basic definite articles are der, die, and das.

mentalModel.title: Articles act like labels
mentalModel.content: A definite article points to a known or specific noun; an indefinite article introduces one nonspecific noun: der Tisch versus ein Tisch.

mentalModel.title: Plural has one definite article
mentalModel.content: In the basic nominative form, all plural nouns use 'die'. There is no plural form of 'ein' or 'eine'.

ruleBlocks.title: Use der, die, and das for specific singular nouns
ruleBlocks.content: The basic definite articles are 'der' for masculine, 'die' for feminine, and 'das' for neuter nouns.

ruleBlocks.title: Use ein and eine for one unspecified item
ruleBlocks.content: Masculine and neuter nouns use 'ein'; feminine nouns use 'eine': ein Tisch, eine Lampe, ein Sofa.

ruleBlocks.title: Use die for definite plurals
ruleBlocks.content: All plural nouns use 'die' in the basic nominative form: die Tische, die Lampen, die Sofas.

ruleBlocks.title: Store the article with the noun
ruleBlocks.content: Gender often cannot be predicted reliably, so learn 'der Tisch' as one vocabulary unit rather than learning 'Tisch' alone.

patterns: ein + masculine or neuter singular noun
sentenceStructure: Use an indefinite article when introducing one object: 'Das ist eine Lampe.'
Use a definite article when referring to the now-known object: 'Die Lampe ist schön.'
The article appears directly before the noun in these basic noun phrases.
Article forms will change in later case lessons; this page focuses on the nominative foundation.

concepts: recognize der, die, das, ein, and eine
learn gender and plural with each noun
apply articles in accusative and dative contexts
use possessive and negative article forms

comparisons.summary: The theme lesson provides concrete nouns and plural forms. This lesson explains the article system attached to those nouns.
Price questions require the correct subject and singular or plural verb form. Knowing the noun and article makes the question easier to build.

examples.de: Das ist ein Tisch. Der Tisch ist groß.
examples.en: That is a table. The table is large.

examples.de: Das ist eine Lampe. Die Lampe ist modern.
examples.en: That is a lamp. The lamp is modern.

examples.de: Das ist ein Sofa. Das Sofa ist bequem.
examples.en: That is a sofa. The sofa is comfortable.

examples.de: Das sind Stühle. Die Stühle sind neu.
examples.en: Those are chairs. The chairs are new.

commonMistakes.reason: Feminine singular nouns use the indefinite article 'eine'.
'Sofa' is a neuter noun and uses 'das'.
German has no plural indefinite article equivalent to 'ein/eine'.

commonMistakes.wrong: Choose the article from natural gender or object shape.
commonMistakes.correct: Learn the grammatical article with the noun.
commonMistakes.reason: Grammatical gender is attached to the word and is often not predictable from meaning.

specialCases: Some noun endings give useful gender clues, but beginners should not depend on guesses.
The article 'die' can mean feminine singular or plural; the noun and context show which one applies.
The forms on this page are nominative. Masculine articles change in the accusative, introduced in A1.1 M5.
tips: Color-code der, die, and das only if you use the colors consistently.
Always review the plural beside the singular noun.
Practice first mention followed by known reference: 'Das ist ein ... Der/Die/Das ... ist ...'.

memoryHooks.title: The article is the noun's name tag
memoryHooks.content: Do not separate the tag from the noun: der Tisch, die Lampe, das Sofa.

memoryHooks.title: Plural gathers under die
memoryHooks.content: Whatever the singular gender, the basic definite plural article is always 'die'.
